serviceDetails.title: What makes underfloor heating good?
paras: Heat rises from the whole floor and spreads evenly across the room, so there are no hot spots near a radiator and no cold corners. You get your wall space back, which helps in kitchens and small bathrooms, and your feet stay warm on cold mornings.
Because the whole floor gives off heat, the system can run at a lower water temperature than radiators while keeping the room just as warm.
serviceDetails.alt: Warm tiled floor with underfloor heating in a Watford home

serviceDetails.title: Wet or electric underfloor heating: which is best?
paras: Wet underfloor heating runs warm water from your boiler through pipes under the floor. It suits larger areas, new builds, extensions and ground floors, and is usually cheaper to run.

Electric underfloor heating uses thin heating mats under the floor finish. It suits single rooms such as bathrooms and small kitchens, where lifting and raising the whole floor is not practical. We advise which type fits your room in your quote.

serviceDetails.title: Does underfloor heating work with any floor?
paras: Most floors, yes. Tile and stone hold heat well and are the best match. Engineered wood and laminate work well with the right system. Carpet can work too, as long as the carpet and underlay are not too thick. We check your chosen floor and advise before we fit.
serviceDetails.alt: Floor finishes suitable for underfloor heating

serviceDetails.title: Is underfloor heating easy to run?
paras: Yes. Each room or zone gets its own thermostat, so you set the warmth you want in each space. Pair the system with a smart control and you can run your heating from your phone.
Underfloor heating takes longer to warm up than radiators, so it works best on a timer set to suit your day. We set this up with you before we leave.

serviceDetails.title: Will underfloor heating work with my boiler?
paras: Most modern boilers can run a wet underfloor heating system. The system connects to your boiler through a manifold, which sends warm water to each zone. We check your boiler size and type first. If your boiler is too small or near the end of its life, we tell you, and can quote for a new boiler as part of the job.

faqs.q: Does underfloor heating work with any floor?
faqs.a: Most floors, yes. Tile and stone hold heat best. We advise on wood and carpet before we fit.

faqs.q: Is underfloor heating cheap to run?
faqs.a: It can be. It warms the room evenly at a lower temperature, which can use less gas over time when run well.

faqs.q: Can you fit underfloor heating in one room only?
faqs.a: Yes. Many customers start with a kitchen or bathroom.

faqs.q: Wet or electric: which is cheaper to run?
faqs.a: Wet systems running from your boiler are usually cheaper to run. Electric systems cost less to fit in a single small room.

faqs.q: Can I have underfloor heating and radiators together?
faqs.a: Yes. Many homes use underfloor heating on the ground floor and radiators upstairs.

faqs.q: Will underfloor heating raise my floor height?
faqs.a: Electric mats add very little height. Wet systems need more depth, which we plan for in new floors and extensions.

faqs.q: How long does underfloor heating take to warm up?
faqs.a: Longer than radiators, so it works best on a timer. We set this up for you.
